2. The contention of the petitioner is that even if the entire allegations are accepted, no offence under Section 420 IPC is made out.
The counsel for the petitioner also takes me through the final report and submitted that the averments would not constitute an offence under Section 420 IPC.

The Senior Counsel who appears for the 2 nd respondent submitted that these are matters of evidence and this Court may not interfere in the matter under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
3.
I do not want to make any observation about the merit of the case.
The petitioner can raise all the contentions raised in this criminal miscellaneous case before the trial court by filing a discharge petition.
If such a discharge petition is filed, there can be a direction to consider the same within a time frame, without insisting the presence of the petitioner.

Therefore, this Criminal Miscellaneous Case is disposed of in the following manner:
1. The petitioner is free to file a discharge petition before the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-II, Mavelikkara, within two weeks from the date of receipt of a stamped certified copy of this order, if charge is not framed.

sentences.text:
2. Once such a discharge petition is received, the Magistrate will consider the same and pass appropriate orders in it, after giving an opportunity of hearing to the petitioner and the Prosecutor concerned, within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of the discharge petition.
3.
